refute.method: Each SAME re-read against the 2002 text, the 2023 pointer row (tests/version-matrix/inventory/<id>.json test-ref) and the row witnesses' source. The test the brief sets for SAME: every part of the 2002 scope is covered by evidence the POINTER ROW already has, and that evidence holds at --std 2002. A part shown only by the reader's own probe, or by a suite test outside the row, is not row evidence. The reader applied that test itself to its DIFFERENT for 2002-FMT-13.16.51.1 (SOURCE). Probes: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/refute-u-53/ (<name>.cob, <name>-2002.out, <name>-2023.out; r.py runs the pinned compiler).

cases.reason: The SIGN row (FMT-13.18.52.2) has three witnesses, and all three refuse a clause written twice: pb486-sign-written-twice (SIGN twice in a data description entry), pb917-data-usage-twice (USAGE twice, no SIGN at all) and pb917-report-group-picture-twice (PICTURE twice; grep finds no SIGN, LEADING, TRAILING or SEPARATE in the file, and at 2002 it fails with COBOL1657 and COBOL2423 about VALUE and PIC). So no row witness accepts any form of the format at 2002: not LEADING or TRAILING, not the optional SIGN IS, not SEPARATE CHARACTER, not SIGN in a report group entry (2002 SR1 names that entry), and not SIGN in a record under a CD (2002 A.1.1). The reader's 'covered' rests on its own probes (sign_sync.cob, cd_clauses.cob), which are not row evidence. The compiler is correct at 2002: the reader's sign_sync.cob and cd_clauses.cob, and my sign_rg.cob, where a report group with SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER and TRAILING SEPARATE prints [-07 07-] at 2002 and at 2023.

cases.reason: In 2002 the identifier-1 addend and the identifiers inside arithmetic-expression-1 may be any non-report-section item, so they include items of a record under a CD. The suite already has a 2002-only case for exactly this, cases/13.16.52@2002-SUM-CLAUSE/g2sum01_sum_cd_addends_timing (SUM CD-N, SUM (CD-N + 1) CD-N WS-B, UPON). It matches its golden at --std 2002 and is refused at 2023 (COBOL0902), but it is not in the row. The row's one positive witness, pb1295_report_sum_groups_then_reset_rounded, writes only `SUM WS-A SUM WS-B RESET ON FINAL ROUNDED`. So the row also never shows a data-name-1 addend (a report-section item, rolling forward), an arithmetic-expression-1 addend, the UPON phrase, or RESET ON data-name-3. The reader used this same gap to rule SOURCE DIFFERENT. At 2002 the compiler is correct for every candidate: g2sum01, pb1294_report_rolled_cross_report (SUM X1 OF RA; SUM WS-A UPON DA OF RA) and pb1297_sum_reset_level_upon_85 (RESET ON WS-C; UPON DE-A DE-A) all match their goldens.

In 2002 a CD entry may be followed by record description entries (A.1.1), so a level-1 TYPEDEF entry under a CD falls within 2002's scope. 2023 has no such context. The row witness l1c34_typedef_format_spellings declares its types only in working storage, and the reader's cd_clauses.cob puts its TYPEDEF in working storage, not under the CD. My probe typedef_cd.cob declares `01 CDT IS TYPEDEF PIC X(3)` and `01 CDS TYPEDEF STRONG` under an output CD and uses them in working storage. At 2002 it compiles (COBOL0903 obsolete warning only) and prints V1=ABC V2=42Z. The compiler is correct, but no row witness covers the case.
